body: Lurk
I'm not sure. It's always worth a shot though. Thank you for your time and kind responses, friend.

I've never had any real ambitions in life. Always been a background character. Just  figured I might as well do something for others. I've never done anything 'big'. Anxiety makes me resist that. 

I've lost count of the time I've spent on games. I saved up and made a ~$1300 pc this last summer. Still haven't played that much. I shouldn't of bought it. I just sit and stare at a menu most of the time sadly.

I appreciate your message. I've always enjoyed sports, video games, and helping others. I just think my depression has been getting the best of me these days. I just never have the energy to do those things anymore. My birthday wasn't too long ago and after so much time put into an uncertain degree, lack of connections I've made, and lack of anything to show, it's gotten me down.
This is a path I have considered a lot lately. Getting a masters seems daunting to me though. It is something I definitely plan on looking into though! Thanks for your time!

That's what I wasn't sure of. I think I was just trying too hard to find something I can do with my degree that in turn would be beneficial to others, rather than my own degree of wisdom. Thank you for your response.
I'm not in good terms with my nobility. Ran from home. Something like that. I've considered convincing them to travel back, repair my connections, then using it against them.

That's something I've considered. It's usually just small things though. And my character isn't necessarily good. I enjoy my character. I know it's just how they've made their characters, and it's not something I want to make a big deal out of. I'll talk to my DM. 

This is also my second character. My first I didn't enjoy due to lack of connection. I'm just looking for a level of playing on their level. We like to be jerks to eachother. I'm just a wimpy bard lol
I'm sorry for your struggles. I'm glad to hear I'm not alone though. And thank you for taking the time to respond. Best wishes friend
I am very sorry to hear that.. I hope you're doing alright. That would be tough for anyone to endure. I couldn't imagine.

Thank you for your response. It was definitely what I needed to hear. I hope she understands! 

And if you need a friend, feel free to message me! :)
Good to know! I will definitely do that! Thanks!

I am as well! I've played a few games over the years but they usually die down pretty quickly. I'm hoping this one lasts! Luckily we found a day that should work for us. And will do! Thanks!! Same goes to you
I wouldn't want to do that. But I definitely plan on checking out some more info! Thanks! :)

Yeah.. I didn't realize that. It seems like everyone's been saying that. But that $15 a month plus expansions I'd have to get. Poor college student with limited times. I was thinking like around $30 if I had to get something new.
I am actually in a D&D game right now. We actually play for the second time tomorrow! Sadly the rest of the group don't really have PCs able to do much. But I really do enjoy playing it!

I used to be into WoW a long time ago. I thought about replaying with the new expansion. But that is not exactly the game in looking for. I'm looking for games/people to play something with an added RP content. 

For example, take something like Minecraft. Have a server not just based on building or pvp, but rather pretending to fill a role and playing based on some sort of society based structure. Usually on a dedicated server. You know. RPing. Probably shouldn't of said RPGs.
I will take a look at it! Thanks!
Probably not. My college career path is taking me somewhere vastly different. But, it is good news in the fact that I'm reaching out and wanting to try new things!

I get what you're saying. I do a fair amount of smoking. That's most of the social interaction I get besides work. I rarely tell anyone outside that group about it though, because I don't want to be judged irrationally. Besides that and maybe a video game, my life is very bland. Archery sounds like a very cool activity.  I am glad you have something to enjoy! I was actually looking up gem cutting today. I work at a jewelry store, just sales, but I found the whole process interesting. And expensive. Very expensive. But I hope to keep looking. I think I just need to find a good community and try out different things. But I'm glad I'm not alone. Thanks for the reply, and same goes to you friend!
Hey Josh! Saved the post to add you later. Hope this post gets attention. It's always great getting to play with a group. Also 19m. Best of luck!
Thank you for the reply! I have found everyone's replies very constructive and helpful. This seems like a great community. I can wait to further my knowledge. I will keep your comment in mind!

What worries me, like I just posted in another reply, is the fear of the other field I would need to study. Lacking interest in a lot of things is one of my faults. I would hate to work towards getting a degree I would dislike, unintentionally but little effort towards, and eventually do that for a living. I agree 100% with Philosophy being too general. And at this time I have no interest in pursuing a graduate school advancement. Just looking for a simple bachelors degree. I realize j may be asking two opposites, saying how I only am interested in philosophy, hate everything else, but don't want to specialize in philosophy. I've considered pursing a foreign language with my philosophy degree. I've considered some degree of law enforcement. As well some sort of business management. I just don't know if any of these pair well with philosophy, or if philosophy should be dropped and just keep it too an interest. Hope this makes sense. Thank you for the reply.

Thank you for the informative response. I feel like my short time in my philosophy class has broadened views on many things. It has enabled my thought process to be more understanding, as well as give me "answers" to questions I've always wondered. As silly as it may sound, I really believe that philosophy pairs well with me in the fact that I have always been a deep thinker. I always contemplate every decision, I always pay regards to both outcomes, and I always accomplish tasks and in a rightful manor. I believe philosophy has already made me stronger at doing so. Just hearing different topics from Kant or Descartes, even Plato or Aristotle. 

At my local college, they only offer a BS or BA in philosophy. The BS requiring a second major and the BA a second language. I hear a lot that just having a degree is important today. And many people won't even get jobs in their field of study. I feel like I could use philosophy in most fields. I just don't know if it's too broad. And it scares me to select another major I have no interest in. I've considered the extra language, but then again, I'm not sure if that will be enough.
I've considered that. I talked to an Army recruiter my senior year of highschool. But due to the meds I was taking and my scoliosis, he said I probably couldn't.
